Key observations: the wd curvature b grows steeply with tokens (0.0006 → 0.0035 → 0.0087 for 0.75B → 3B → 6B), so wd will matter a lot at 48B. Let me fit candidate scaling forms for lr* to extrapolate to (4096, 48B).

python3 - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
# lr* estimates (B, D, lr*) ; (256,6) corrected for fixed-wd shift
data=[(256,0.75,0.1178),(256,3,0.02623),(256,6,0.0113),(256,48,0.000756),(1024,0.75,0.16046),(4096,0.75,0.16682),(4096,3,0.07233),(4096,6,0.04628)]
B=np.array([d[0] for d in data],float);D=np.array([d[1] for d in data]);y=np.log([d[2] for d in data])
def fitform(name,f,p0):
    # simple Nelder-Mead
    def loss(p): return np.sum((f(p,B,D)-y)**2)
    p=np.array(p0,float); 
    # crude random-restart coordinate descent
    best=loss(p)
    for it in range(20000):
        q=p+np.random.randn(len(p))*0.05*(0.999**it+0.01)
        l=loss(q)
        if l<best: best,p=l,q
    pred=f(p,np.array([4096.]),np.array([48.]))
    print(f"{name}: rms={np.sqrt(best/len(y)):.3f} params={np.round(p,3)} pred lr*(4096,48)={np.exp(pred[0]):.5f}")
    print("   resid:",np.round(y-f(p,B,D),3))
np.random.seed(0)
fitform("powerlaw", lambda p,B,D: p[0]+p[1]*np.log(B/256)+p[2]*np.log(D/48), [-7,0.5,-1])
fitform("linsat Bc=kD^d", lambda p,B,D: p[0]+p[1]*np.log(D/48)+np.log(B/256)-np.log(1+B/(np.exp(p[2])*D**p[3])), [-7,-1,6,1])
fitform("linsat Bc=kD", lambda p,B,D: p[0]+p[1]*np.log(D/48)+np.log(B/256)-np.log(1+B/(np.exp(p[2])*D)), [-7,-1,6])
fitform("powsat", lambda p,B,D: p[0]+p[1]*np.log(D/48)+p[4]*(np.log(B/256)-np.log(1+B/(np.exp(p[2])*D**p[3]))), [-7,-1,6,1,1])
fitform("quad in logD + B", lambda p,B,D: p[0]+p[1]*np.log(D/48)+p[2]*np.log(D/48)**2+p[3]*np.log(B/256)+p[4]*np.log(B/256)*np.log(D/48), [-7,-1,0,0.5,0])
EOF
